strengths: Novel identification and formal characterization of Marginal Path Collapse as a systematic failure mode in heterogeneous expert composition, affecting 41%-80% of schedule combinations

Rigorous theoretical framework with sharp path existence criterion (PEC) and constructive guarantees for the ACE correction method, with complete proofs connecting Feynman-Kac dynamics to practical diffusion steering
Practical algorithm that requires no retraining or architectural changes while maintaining endpoint distribution validity, validated across multiple molecular generation tasks with 4× error reduction

Comprehensive experimental validation including synthetic benchmarks, real molecular tasks (scaffold decoration, fragment linking), and quantitative analysis across 100+ heterogeneous combinations with consistent improvements
Excellent reproducibility with provided source code, fixed random seeds, detailed hyperparameters, and reproducibility statement covering all experiments
weaknesses: Limited experimental scope primarily focused on molecular generation with only 2D synthetic benchmark; missing evaluation on standard image generation benchmarks (COCO, ImageNet) familiar to ICML community
Lack of principled guidance for hyperparameter selection (B₁, B₂) in the bump function correction; while sensitivity analysis is provided, practitioners lack clear guidelines for new tasks

Gap between theoretical guarantees (PEC criterion assuming compact support/Gaussian tails) and practical algorithm (adaptive bump functions); some theoretical assumptions may not hold for all real-world distributions and non-Gaussian priors are left as future work

Incomplete cost-benefit analysis: computational cost scales linearly with expert count, practical limits unexplored, and paper doesn't discuss when ACE should be used vs. alternatives (single homogeneous model, alternative weighting schemes, or cases where collapse has negligible impact)

Insufficient discussion in main text of failure mode consequences: functional vs. distributional failures are documented in appendix but key practical insights (predicting affected tasks, quantifying impact) remain underdeveloped

strengths: Identifies and formally characterizes an important and previously overlooked failure mode (Marginal Path Collapse) in diffusion steering for heterogeneous expert composition, with rigorous theoretical analysis (Theorems 2.1-2.3)
Provides a principled diagnostic tool (Path Existence Criterion) and a theoretically grounded solution (ACE) with detailed proofs covering Gaussian mixture models and integrability conditions
Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse domains (synthetic benchmarks, molecular docking, protein design tasks) with systematic ablation studies and sensitivity analyses
Strong reproducibility support including detailed algorithms, hyperparameters in appendices, and explicit reproducibility statement with implementation details
Clear motivating examples (Gaussian path collapse in Example A.1) effectively communicate the problem before formal treatment
weaknesses: Limited scope: The problem is specific to ratio-of-densities steering with heterogeneous experts; applicability is narrow compared to general diffusion steering and doesn't extend to other generative model architectures

Restrictive theoretical assumptions: Theorem 2.1 requires compactly supported intermediate distributions, significantly limiting applicability to realistic scenarios with unbounded or heavy-tailed distributions (acknowledged as future work)

Modest empirical improvements: Performance gains over baselines are consistent but often marginal (typically 1-2% on key metrics with overlapping error bars in Tables 2-4), limiting practical significance despite statistical consistency

Dense mathematical presentation with heavy notation (σᵢ⁽ⁱ⁾, γᵢ(t), etc.) that obscures the main insights; key implementation details relegated to 35-page appendix, reducing accessibility to non-specialists

Complex implementation with multiple moving parts: Bump function construction, adaptive exponent scheduling, resampling logic, and hyperparameter selection add practical overhead; numerical stability of derivative-based criterion C(t) not thoroughly addressed

FKC paradox not fully resolved: The paper notes FKC remains numerically computable when MPC occurs (page 21); the distinction is theoretical (sampling from unintended path) but practical significance unclear since FKC produces reasonable empirical results

Limited experimental scope: Improvements shown primarily on molecular design tasks; scaling to larger domains (e.g., language models, large-scale vision) untested; some experimental choices appear optimized for ACE (e.g., guidance scale selection in Figure C.3)

strengths: Novel identification and formal characterization of Marginal Path Collapse as a failure mode in heterogeneous diffusion model composition
Rigorous theoretical contributions including the sharp Path Existence Criterion (Theorem 2.1) with detailed proofs connecting to ratio-of-densities steering
Practical Adaptive Path Correction with Exponents (ACE) method that consistently improves sampling quality across multiple domains

Comprehensive experimental validation spanning synthetic benchmarks (2D checker), scientific applications (scaffold decoration, fragment linking), and image generation with appropriate baselines and multiple metrics
Honest and thorough treatment of limitations with extensive analysis in Appendix E including systematic prevalence study of collapse across 125 heterogeneous schedule combinations
Strong reproducibility support with detailed hyperparameters, noise schedules, and algorithmic specifications in appendices; code release promised
General theoretical framework (heterogeneous ratio-of-densities composition) with applicability beyond tested domains
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty of the correction method: ACE uses relatively straightforward time-varying exponent schedules rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Restrictive mathematical assumptions (compactly supported distributions, Gaussian interpolants) limit applicability to specific distribution classes
Presentation complexity: dense mathematical exposition in main text makes paper less accessible; critical results (e.g., Table E.10-E.11) buried in appendices
Incomplete practical guidance: lacking principled methods for selecting exponent schedules or bump function parameters (B₁, B₂) beyond task-specific tuning
Scope limitations: primarily addresses heterogeneous composition scenarios with specialized applicability; most realistic applications detailed are fragment linking
Computational cost-benefit analysis missing: overhead of ACE resampling step relative to performance gains not thoroughly quantified
Method dependencies: requires access to individual expert densities and computation of path criterion C(t), which may not be available in all practical scenarios
